title: Wallet activated, but rarely used to pay
disclaimer: Practice scenario. The company is fictional and every figure is hypothetical. Australian market context is general.
company_context: TapLoop (fictional) is an Australian digital wallet that combines saved cards and loyalty points for a network of retail partners, with in-store QR and online checkout.

brief.problem: Customers activate the TapLoop wallet, but fewer of them use it to pay.
brief.objective: Lift monthly active payers from 18% to 30% of activated users within six months.
baseline: Monthly active payers: 18% of activated users, down from 26% a year ago.

facts.answer: TapLoop earns about $0.45 per wallet payment from partner fees, and active payers make about 6 payments a month. The 8-point drop is about 17,600 fewer payers — roughly $47k a month, or about $570k a year.
facts.coach_tip: Size it, then add the strategic risk: partners judge us on usage.
facts.model_question: What's the revenue impact of fewer active payers?

facts.answer: A monthly active payer makes at least one successful wallet payment in a calendar month. Opening the app without paying doesn't count.
facts.coach_tip: This tells you the problem is paying, not opening the app.
facts.model_question: How is a monthly active payer defined?

facts.answer: In-store QR payers fell from 20% to 11% of activated users. Online checkout payers held steady at about 7%. Some customers use both.
facts.coach_tip: The drop is in-store — focus there.
facts.model_question: Is the drop in-store, online or both?

facts.answer: App opens are steady at about 9 a month per user, mostly to check points. 63% of in-store payment attempts that start don't complete.
facts.coach_tip: Customers are trying to pay and failing — that's not low interest.
facts.model_question: What are customers actually doing in the app?

facts.answer: Last month in-store: open app at till 100% → QR shown 86% → scanned by terminal 71% → payment authorised 46% (was 78%) → receipt and points 45%.
facts.coach_tip: The biggest drop is authorisation: 78% to 46%.
facts.model_question: Can I see the in-store payment funnel, step by step?

facts.answer: Android users' authorisation rate is 39%; iOS is 58%.
facts.coach_tip: Both are well below the old 78%, so it's not just one platform.
facts.model_question: Does the drop differ between Android and iOS?

facts.answer: Five months ago an app release added step-up authentication: a biometric check plus a one-time SMS code for every in-store payment, after a fraud review.
facts.coach_tip: Connect this to the authorisation drop.
facts.model_question: Did anything change in the payment flow or security?

facts.answer: App rating fell from 4.6 to 3.8. Reviews and calls: too many steps at the till 47%, SMS code arrives late 29%, QR won't scan 14%. Store staff report queues backing up.
facts.coach_tip: Two themes cover 76% — both point to the extra step.
facts.model_question: What are customers and store staff saying?

facts.answer: Fraud losses were 0.04% of payment value before the change and 0.03% after. Most fraud came from new devices in their first 7 days.
facts.coach_tip: This is your key to a targeted fix — and your guardrail.
facts.model_question: What fraud problem was the change solving?

facts.answer: Points rates haven't changed. A partner promotion ended last quarter, but active payers were already falling before it ended.
facts.coach_tip: Good to rule out — the timing doesn't fit.
facts.model_question: Did any loyalty or partner offers change?

facts.answer: Estimates: faster SMS provider — 2 weeks. Show the QR before reaching the till — 4 weeks. Risk-based step-up, only for new devices or high-value payments — 5 weeks, needs fraud team sign-off.
facts.coach_tip: Map these to options and weigh impact vs effort.
facts.model_question: What are our options and estimates?

model_answer.problem_statement: In-store wallet users are abandoning at payment authorisation — authorisation fell from 78% to 46% — because every in-store payment now needs a biometric check plus a one-time SMS code, so monthly active payers fell from 26% to 18% of activated users.

options.name: Faster SMS provider
options.description: Switch to a faster SMS provider for one-time codes.
options.why: Quick, but keeps the extra step.

options.name: Risk-based step-up
options.description: Ask for the extra check only on new devices or high-value payments.
options.customer_impact: Most payments go back to one tap.
options.business_impact: Targets 76% of complaints; could recover most of the 8-point drop.
options.why: Removes friction where fraud risk is low.

options.name: QR before the till
options.description: Let customers open their QR before reaching the counter.
options.business_impact: Shorter queues; doesn't fix the extra code.
options.why: Nice add-on, not the root cause.

model_answer.decision: Build risk-based step-up with the fraud team in 5 weeks, so only new devices and high-value payments need the extra code, and switch SMS providers now as a quick win.
model_answer.hypothesis: If we apply step-up only to new devices and high-value payments, in-store authorisation will rise from 46% to 70%+ and monthly active payers from 18% to 26% within two quarters, because the drop began with blanket step-up and most fraud comes from new devices.
model_answer.test: Staged rollout: 20% of trusted-device users get risk-based step-up for 4 weeks vs a control group.
guardrails: Fraud losses as % of payment value
